To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the structural phase diagram of a material is a fundamental design tool to predict and realize the synthesis of novel materials with enhanced properties and (2) heterostructural alloys are a class of materials with novel phase diagram properties, and they can be realized in thin-films.
heterostructural alloying provides a novel approach to design materials with unprecedented properties by tuning the composition and structure.
heterostructural semiconducting alloys can exhibit novel phase diagram behavior and that the properties change in an extremely nonlinear or even discontinuously fashion as a function of composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and discovery of new materials with desired properties.
the design and synthesis of novel materials by means of heterostructural alloying.
the synthesis, characterization, and theory of novel metastable heterostructural alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phase diagram of heterostructural semiconductor alloy systems can be extended to the composition range where the phase separation occurs in the isostructural alloy systems.
the phase diagram of heterostructural semiconductor alloy is fundamentally different than that of isostructural alloy and provides a novel approach to materials design.
the heterostructural alloys have the ability to create new materials with novel and tunable properties that cannot be realized by conventional methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heterostructural alloying is a promising strategy for materials design, which can provide a new class of materials with unprecedented functionality and tunability.
the structural transition is a powerful mechanism to control the phase diagram of alloys.
we have shown that the structure and composition of a material can be used as a design tool for the control and tuning of its properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase diagram of a heterostructural alloy can exhibit a much wider range of metastable alloys than that of a conventional isostructural alloy.
a new phase diagram behavior is possible by alloying between different structures, which is of fundamental interest and may be exploited in materials design.

a novel type of heterostructural alloying can lead to a much larger range of single-phase compositions than is possible in conventional alloys and that this approach is applicable to many other materials systems, thereby providing a new route to materials design.
